title: AI RESILIENCE evidence-grounded disaster knowledge
purpose: General disaster preparedness information and source navigation. Not a live warning feed, local forecast, or substitute for official instructions.

topics.title: Flood preparedness
topics.summary: Flood impacts depend on rainfall, catchment response, drainage, river or coastal conditions, terrain, and local infrastructure. Do not infer a street- or ward-level flood probability from a statewide hazard map alone.
actions: Follow current instructions and warnings from the competent local and state authorities.
Avoid walking or driving through floodwater; depth, current, and road condition may be unknown.
Keep essential medicines, drinking water, charged communication devices, and important documents ready where appropriate.
Report blocked drains or damaged infrastructure to the responsible local authority; do not enter drains or floodwater to inspect them.
limitations: This assistant has no verified live flood observations or operational forecast.
The current project flood raster has unresolved pixel semantics and reuse terms, so it is not used to calculate local depth or probability.

topics.title: Cyclone preparedness
topics.summary: Cyclone impacts may include destructive winds, intense rainfall, coastal flooding, power or communication disruption, and blocked access. Actual local impacts depend on the official forecast and local conditions.
actions: Use official IMD bulletins and local-authority instructions for timing and evacuation decisions.
Secure loose outdoor objects only when it is safe to do so; do not go outside during dangerous conditions.
Plan for power, communications, drinking water, medicines, and essential-service disruption.
Treat cyclone-plus-flood impacts as a compound scenario; this prototype does not calculate joint probabilities.
limitations: No live cyclone warning feed is connected to this assistant.
Do not use this assistant to decide whether to evacuate; follow official instructions.

topics.title: Earthquake preparedness
topics.summary: Earthquake consequences depend on shaking, soil conditions, building design and condition, and exposed people and services. This app cannot certify the safety of any building.
actions: Identify safe places and exits in advance and practise an age-appropriate household or school plan.
During shaking, follow recognised protective guidance such as Drop, Cover, and Hold On where appropriate; stay away from windows.
After shaking, avoid damaged structures and follow emergency-service instructions.
Have structural safety concerns assessed by qualified engineers, not by this app.
limitations: No building inventory, site-specific seismic assessment, or structural inspection is connected.
The assistant does not estimate earthquake probability or building damage.

topics.title: Air pollution and industrial source attribution
topics.summary: AQI describes air-quality conditions using measured pollutant information; it does not by itself identify a particular factory as the source. Attribution needs pollutant-specific measurements, reliable station locations and times, meteorology, and facility emissions or other source evidence.
actions: Check the date, station, pollutant, units, averaging period, and data-completeness notes for each measurement.
Compare multiple time-aligned observations and meteorological conditions before drawing source hypotheses.
Treat a possible facility source as a hypothesis for investigation, not a proven cause.
Use the responsible pollution-control authority's monitoring and complaint channels for official investigation.
limitations: The current project does not establish a scientifically validated factory-attribution result.
Historical station summaries must not be described as live AQI.

topics.title: Landslide and slope-failure preparedness
topics.summary: Landslide risk depends on rainfall, slope material, drainage, vegetation, excavation, and prior slope movement. The project holds only a small, media-reported historical catalogue and an unusable local susceptibility layer, so it does not assign a landslide class to a ward, road, or slope.
actions: Follow official KSDMA, IMD, and district-administration warnings; do not treat this assistant as an early-warning service.
Avoid hill roads and steep slopes during intense or prolonged rainfall, especially where cracks, leaning trees, tilted poles, or new springs are visible.
If authorities advise evacuation, leave early by a safe route; do not wait for the slope to fail.
Refer any slope-stability concern to a qualified geotechnical authority for site assessment; do not rely on a statewide map to certify local safety.
limitations: The project's GSI susceptibility polygons fail geometry validity checks and cannot be used for local classification.
The NASA Global Landslide Catalog entries naming Ernakulam are historical examples with reporting bias and stated coordinate uncertainty, not a complete event inventory or frequency estimate.
This assistant cannot predict when or where a specific slope will fail.

topics.title: Cyclone, storm, heatwave and lightning preparedness
topics.summary: Cyclones, severe storms, heatwaves, and lightning can disrupt power, communications, transport, water, and health services. The project holds regional storm-track context but no validated Ernakulam impact series, so it does not estimate local wind, storm-surge, heat, or lightning likelihood.
actions: Use official IMD bulletins and KSDMA or district instructions for alert interpretation and evacuation decisions.
Secure loose outdoor objects only when it is safe; stay indoors during high winds and lightning and avoid trees, poles, and open ground.
Plan for power, communication, drinking-water, medicine, and transport disruption, including backup arrangements for critical services.
During extreme heat, reduce outdoor exertion, check on vulnerable people, and use cooling or hydration measures consistent with official heat-action guidance.
limitations: Regional IBTrACS track positions do not establish Ernakulam landfall, local wind, storm surge, rainfall, damage, or district impact.
No live weather feed is connected; the assistant cannot issue or confirm a warning.
Heat and lightning advice is general preparedness guidance, not a local forecast.

topics.title: Industrial and chemical incident preparedness
topics.summary: Industrial and chemical incidents can release toxic, flammable, or asphyxiant substances and may be worsened by flooding or fire. The project contains general industrial-area context and dated air monitoring, but no validated facility incident inventory, safe-distance model, or source-attribution result.
actions: For an active release, call 112 or 101, move away and upwind if it is safe, and follow official evacuation or shelter-in-place instructions.
Do not re-enter an affected area or attempt to identify the substance yourself; wait for the responding authority.
Report the location, visible plume or odour, and symptoms to emergency services without approaching the source.
Facilities should maintain process-hazard analysis, emergency plans, drills, and coordination with the pollution-control and fire authorities.
limitations: The project does not calculate a safe evacuation distance, plume extent, or facility-specific risk.
Air-quality measurements cannot by themselves identify the facility responsible for a release.
No verified Ernakulam industrial-incident event series is available in the project.

topics.title: Hospital and health-service preparedness
topics.summary: Hospital preparedness covers continuity of power, water, oxygen, communications, staffing, supplies, access routes, and patient evacuation. The project has a hospital directory review and a normal-condition network cache, but no validated facility vulnerability ranking or disaster-time accessibility result.
actions: Review continuity plans for power, water, oxygen, medical gases, communications, and essential supplies, including backup duration and fuel arrangements.
Identify alternate access routes and ambulance pick-up points, and coordinate them with district authorities and neighbouring facilities.
Plan patient evacuation, surge capacity, triage, infection control, and decontamination with the responsible health authorities.
Record the source, date, scope, and validation status of facility data before using it for planning; resolve coordinate and operational-status gaps first.
limitations: All reviewed NIHFW coordinate rows are marked NOT VALIDATED; coordinate order, CRS, and positional quality are not established.
The network cache covers normal-condition drive times with assumed speeds and no observed traffic; it is not a disaster-time accessibility assessment.
No validated hospital vulnerability ranking exists in the project because facility hazard, structural, continuity, and scoring evidence are incomplete.

topics.title: Mitigation, budget and preparedness planning
topics.summary: Mitigation planning links a documented risk to a candidate intervention, an evidence basis, a cost basis, technical review, and maintenance. The project's catalogue contains guideline candidates only; it does not rank effectiveness or certify that a funded project will reduce risk.
actions: State the hazard, location, exposed assets, and decision trigger before selecting an intervention.
Record a source, date, scope, and unit basis for every cost; treat 'Cost unknown' as a gap rather than zero cost.
Require technical review and geotechnical, hydrological, or engineering assessment before approving a project.
Include maintenance, monitoring, co-benefits, and residual risk, and prefer low-regret measures that are robust to uncertainty.
limitations: The 13 catalogue records are guideline candidates with 'Cost unknown' status; the budget page performs arithmetic on user-entered estimates only.
No validated local effectiveness ranking or benefit-cost result is available.
A project fitting a budget does not prove technical feasibility or risk reduction.

topics.title: Compound disasters and critical services
topics.summary: When hazards overlap, one event may reduce access, power, communications, drainage, or healthcare capacity needed to respond to another. The sequence and shared dependencies matter; separate hazard probabilities must not simply be multiplied without a justified joint model.
actions: List each hazard, its timing, what is observed versus assumed, and the source for each input.
Review dependencies across hospitals, roads, power, water, communications, shelters, and drainage.
Record alternate access, backup duration, responsible operators, and decision triggers from official plans.
Keep uncertain consequences qualitative until local impact records and a validated method are available.
limitations: The compound-scenario worksheet is qualitative and does not estimate casualties, damage, outage duration, or joint probability.
Hospital locations, flood exposure, and access routes are not yet approved for definitive ward-level claims.
